ai.literal: Is it evening? You are not. Those who united, life-consuming time you are, may you live, O time!
ai.translation: You are not just the evening; you are the life-consuming hour for those who once united. May you prosper, O twilight hour!
ai.modern: பொழுதே! நீ வெறும் மாலைப் பொழுது அல்ல; கூடிப் பிரிந்தவர்களின் உயிரைக் குடிக்கும் கொலைக் காலம் நீ; நீ வாழ்க!
ai.explanation: The heroine, suffering from the pain of separation, addresses the approaching evening. She declares that this hour is not a gentle evening (மாலை) but rather a deadly time (வேலை) that devours the lives of lovers who are separated. The word 'வேலை' primarily means 'time' or 'season', but it also evokes the image of a sharp spear (வேல்) that inflicts a mortal wound. By addressing the evening with the ironic blessing 'வாழி' (may you live), she expresses her deep anguish and resentment toward this painful period of the day.

ai.literal: You are sorrowful, may you live, bewildering evening! Like my lover, is it hard-hearted, your companion?
ai.translation: May you live long, O bewildering evening! You look so sorrowful. Is your companion too as hard-hearted as my lover?
ai.modern: மயக்கம் தரும் மாலையே! நீ வாழ்க! நீ துன்பத்துடன் காணப்படுகிறாய். என் காதலனைப் போல உன்னுடைய துணையும் இரக்கமற்ற நெஞ்சத்தைக் கொண்டிருக்கிறதா?
ai.explanation: The heroine, suffering from the pain of separation, addresses the evening twilight. She notices that the evening seems dim and sorrowful, just like her. She asks the evening if its own companion, the sun which has departed, is as cruel and hard-hearted as her own lover who has left her. The word 'puṉkaṇ' (sorrow) denotes the sad appearance of the evening, while 'vaṉkaṇ' (hard-heartedness) highlights the perceived cruelty of the departing companion.

ai.literal: Cold dew budding, distress having evening, intense grief budding, suffering to grow, comes.
ai.translation: The evening, which arrives shedding cold dew and bringing distress, comes budding with intense grief to make my suffering grow.
ai.modern: குளிர்ச்சியான பனித்துளிகளைச் சிந்தி, துன்பத்தைத் தரும் மாலைப் பொழுது, என் நெஞ்சில் வெறுப்பைத் தோற்றுவித்துத் துயரத்தை வளர்க்கும் வகையில் வருகிறது.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the painful arrival of evening for a heroine separated from her lover. The poet beautifully uses the word 'அரும்பி' (budding) twice to draw a parallel between nature and emotion. First, the evening arrives 'budding' with cold dew (பனி அரும்பி), which physically chills the environment and brings distress (பைதல்). Second, as this evening advances, it causes intense grief or resentment (துனி) to 'bud' (அரும்பி) within her heart, causing her overall suffering (துன்பம்) to grow even larger.

ai.literal: When the lover is absent, evening, like hostile strangers on an execution ground, comes.
ai.translation: In the absence of my lover, the evening arrives like ruthless executioners entering a killing ground.
ai.modern: காதலர் இல்லாதபோது, மாலைப் பொழுது கொலைக்களத்தில் வரும் பகைவர்களைப் போலக் கொடியதாக வருகிறது.
ai.explanation: This couplet captures the deep anguish of a woman separated from her partner as night falls. The evening, which would normally be a time of joyful reunion, becomes a source of immense torment in his absence. The poet compares the arrival of evening to the arrival of hostile executioners (ஏதிலர்) on a killing field (கொலைக்களம்). Just as executioners bring swift and merciless death to those on the scaffold, the onset of evening ruthlessly assaults the lonely heroine's heart.

ai.literal: To the morning done good what indeed? What indeed I to the evening done enmity?
ai.translation: What good did I do to the morning, and what enmity did I commit against the evening, that the former is so kind and the latter so cruel?
ai.modern: நான் காலைப் பொழுதிற்குச் செய்த நன்மை என்னவோ? மாலைப் பொழுதிற்கு நான் செய்த பகைமைதான் என்னவோ?
ai.explanation: The pining heroine compares her feelings during different times of the day. The morning is gentle and does not torment her, making her wonder what good deed she did to earn its favor. In contrast, the evening arrives like a fierce enemy, intensifying her pain of separation, which makes her wonder what enmity she committed against it. Through this personification of morning and evening, the couplet beautifully illustrates how twilight amplifies the grief of those separated from their beloved.

ai.literal: Evening-affliction causing, my lover not-departing morning, I did not know.
ai.translation: In the morning, when my beloved had not departed from me, I did not know that the evening would bring such painful affliction.
ai.modern: என் கணவர் என்னை விட்டுப் பிரியாத காலைப் பொழுதில், மாலைப் பொழுது இத்தகைய துன்பத்தைத் தரும் என்பதை நான் அறிந்திருக்கவில்லை.
ai.explanation: The heroine, suffering from the pain of separation, laments the arrival of the evening. She reflects on the morning when her lover was still by her side, a time of joy and security. At that time, she could not have anticipated how agonizing the evening would become once he departed. The contrast between 'காலை' (morning) and 'மாலை' (evening) highlights how quickly her state of mind shifted from happiness to deep sorrow.

ai.literal: In the morning budding, all through the day becoming a half-open bud, in the evening blossoms this affliction.
ai.translation: This affliction of love buds in the morning, grows into a half-open bud all through the day, and fully blossoms in the evening.
ai.modern: இந்தக் காம நோய் காலையில் அரும்பாகி, பகல் முழுவதும் மொட்டாகி, மாலையில் முழுமையாக மலர்கிறது.
ai.explanation: The heroine describes her painful longing using the metaphor of a flower's growth cycle. In the morning, when she wakes up, the pain begins to bud. Throughout the day, as she manages to distract herself, it slowly grows into a half-open bud. Finally, when evening arrives, the pain fully blossoms and becomes unbearable. This vivid imagery illustrates how her grief intensifies progressively with the passage of time each day.

ai.literal: Becoming a messenger to the fire-resembling evening, the shepherd's flute indeed is a killing weapon.
ai.translation: Serving as a messenger to the evening that burns like fire, the shepherd's flute has become a weapon that kills me.
ai.modern: நெருப்பைப் போன்ற மாலைப் பொழுதுக்குத் தூதாக வந்து, ஆயனுடைய புல்லாங்குழல் ஓசை என்னைக் கொல்லும் ஆயுதமாக மாறுகிறது.
ai.explanation: In this verse, the heroine laments her state of separation during the evening. She describes the evening as a burning fire ('அழல்') because of the intense pain of loneliness it brings. The sound of the shepherd's flute ('ஆயன் குழல்'), which traditionally signals the return of herds at dusk, now sounds to her like a herald or messenger ('தூது') announcing the arrival of this painful evening. Consequently, the sweet music of the flute is transformed in her mind into a lethal weapon ('கொல்லும் படை') that destroys her life.

ai.literal: At the time when evening spreads, bewildering the mind, the town, having become bewildered, suffers distress.
ai.translation: At the hour when evening spreads, bewildering my mind, the entire town itself seems bewildered and suffers in deep distress.
ai.modern: என் அறிவு மயங்கும்படியாக மாலைப் பொழுது வந்து பரவும்போது, இந்த ஊரே மயங்கித் துன்பத்தில் உழல்கிறது.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the lady describes the agonizing arrival of evening during separation. When evening (mālai) spreads (paṭartarum) at that specific time (pōḻtu), it bewilders (maruṇṭu) her mind (mati). In her intense grief, she projects her own sorrow onto her surroundings, perceiving that the entire town (pati) has also become bewildered (maruṇṭu) and is suffering (uḻakkum) in deep distress (paital). The repetition of the word 'maruṇṭu' (bewildered) emphasizes the overwhelming confusion and pain that the twilight hour brings to those separated from their loved ones.

ai.literal: Thinking of the husband whose nature is the pursuit of wealth, in this bewildering evening, my un-perishing life perishes.
ai.translation: Thinking of my beloved whose sole pursuit is wealth, my otherwise un-perishing life now perishes in this bewildering evening.
ai.modern: பொருளையே இயல்பாகக் கொண்ட என் தலைவரை நினைத்து, இந்த மயக்கத்தைத் தரும் மாலைப் பொழுதில், அழியாத என் உயிர் அழிகின்றது.
ai.explanation: The heroine laments her state of separation as twilight falls. She thinks of her husband, who has left her to pursue wealth, describing him as one whose nature is bound to wealth. As she remembers him, the bewildering and sorrowful evening hour overcomes her. Her life, which had stubbornly survived the pain of separation until now, finally begins to fade away under the weight of this evening grief.
